title: Barred Spiral Galaxy NGC 1300
caption: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 1300, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 1300 · constellation Eridanus · about 69 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA); Acknowledgment: P. Knezek (WIYN)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: A straight bar of stars runs through the middle of NGC 1300, with spiral arms sweeping out from each end, crossed by dark dust lanes and studded with resolved supergiants, clusters and star-forming regions. This barred spiral, roughly 69 million light-years away toward the constellation Eridanus, is considered a prototype of its class.

In a barred spiral the arms do not wind all the way into the middle. They attach instead to the two ends of a bar that holds the nucleus at its center. At the heart of NGC 1300 the nucleus has its own grand-design spiral, about 3,300 light-years long, a spiral within a spiral. Only galaxies with large-scale bars seem to have one.

Models suggest that a bar can funnel gas inward, where it may spiral down through the inner disc and feed a central black hole. The galaxy is not known to have an active nucleus, though, so either it has no black hole or its black hole is not taking in matter.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys used four filters, with F435W shown in blue, F555W in green, and near-infrared F814W plus hydrogen-alpha (F658N) in red, so star clusters glowing with hydrogen stand out in red.
understand.eye: Part of the red channel is near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and the red highlights single out the glow of hydrogen gas around bright clusters.

explore: Many more distant galaxies show in the background, even through the densest parts of NGC 1300. The galaxy is so large that Hubble had to point at two neighboring patches of sky to cover its spiral arms. The full image was printed at 4 feet by 8 feet for its unveiling at an American Astronomical Society meeting in San Diego.

alt: A barred spiral galaxy with a straight central bar, curving arms laced with dark dust lanes, and red-highlighted star clusters.
